## 1. Chapter 33: Solution development and integration > 33.6 How to manage development and integration > 33.6.2 Preparing to develop and integrate the solution > 33.6.2.4 Make sure the management information systems are adequate
Source: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government (`teal-book`), Government Project Delivery. Authority: advisory. text last seen to change 2026-10-15 (re-read weekly from the publisher's daily PDF).
Cite inline as: ([The Teal Book: Project delivery in government: 33.6.2.4 Make sure the management information systems are adequate](https://projectdelivery.gov.uk/teal-book/home/part-f-solution-delivery/chapter-33-solution-development-and-integration/#:~:text=33.6.2.4%20Make%20sure%20the%20management%20information%20systems%20are%20adequate,-Management%20information%20systems))

Obligations in this section (verbatim, strength from the modal verb):
- [RECOMMENDED] "Management information systems for tracking risks, issues, change control and traceability should be established before development work starts, as should information systems for tracking verification and validation (see Chapter 24: Information and data management)."

Section text (verbatim):
> Management information systems for tracking risks, issues, change control and traceability should be established before development work starts, as should information systems for tracking verification and validation (see Chapter 24: Information and data management).
> When development work starts, the measures and tools for tracking and reporting progress are likely to need updating to accommodate new types of work. In technology and engineering work, specialist systems are often needed to track the identification and resolution of defects found as a result of verification failures. Such systems are important throughout the life cycle of the work, and are particularly important during delivery before its transition into use.

## 2. Chapter 34: Verification and validation > 34.6 How to manage verification and validation > 34.6.2 Preparing for verification and validation > 34.6.2.3 Prepare the management information systems
Source: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government (`teal-book`), Government Project Delivery. Authority: advisory. text last seen to change 2026-10-15 (re-read weekly from the publisher's daily PDF).
Cite inline as: ([The Teal Book: Project delivery in government: 34.6.2.3 Prepare the management information systems](https://projectdelivery.gov.uk/teal-book/home/part-f-solution-delivery/chapter-34-verification-and-validation/#:~:text=34.6.2.3%20Prepare%20the%20management%20information%20systems,-Management%20information%20systems%2C))

Obligations in this section (verbatim, strength from the modal verb):
- [RECOMMENDED] "Management information systems, whether automated or manual, should be set up to track the results of the planned verification and validation activities."
- [RECOMMENDED] "Overall reporting should be designed to track the results in real time as part of doing the work, or they risk being seen as an administrative burden and fall into disuse (see Chapter 18: Reporting)."

Section text (verbatim):
> Management information systems, whether automated or manual, should be set up to track the results of the planned verification and validation activities. Specialist applications are usually used for specific types of output but the results need to be able to be pulled together to gain an overview of how well work is proceeding at a programme or project level. Overall reporting should be designed to track the results in real time as part of doing the work, or they risk being seen as an administrative burden and fall into disuse (see Chapter 18: Reporting).

## 3. Chapter 17: Controlling > 17.6 How to control the work > 17.6.1 What to consider when controlling the work > 17.6.1.7 Verifying the information
Source: The Teal Book: Project delivery in government (`teal-book`), Government Project Delivery. Authority: advisory. text last seen to change 2026-10-15 (re-read weekly from the publisher's daily PDF).
Cite inline as: ([The Teal Book: Project delivery in government: 17.6.1.7 Verifying the information](https://projectdelivery.gov.uk/teal-book/home/part-e-planning-and-control/chapter-17-controlling/#:~:text=17.6.1.7%20Verifying%20the%20information,-Check.%20Does%20the))

Section text (verbatim):
> Check. Does the information presented make sense? Has it changed since the last report? When was it actually updated? Don’t just rely on the formal information channels. Talk to people, listen to people. Gauge whether what they say really reflects what is being reported. Look at physical progress to see if it reflects the information provided. Be visible and available for people to talk to informally; don’t wait for them to come to you.

## 4. Do not store information any longer than you need to
Source: Service Manual (`service-manual`), Government Digital Service. Authority: advisory. page last updated 2025-03-25, over a year ago.
Cite inline as: ([Service Manual: Do not store information any longer than you need to](https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/design/collecting-personal-information-from-users#do-not-store-information-any-longer-than-you-need-to))

Section text (verbatim):
> You do not always need to store personal information at all. For example, let’s say you need to know if someone is getting a particular benefit so you can tell whether they’re eligible to use your service.
> You may be able to use an application programming interface (API) or something similar to an API so you can just record whether they were eligible or not. And avoid storing the raw personal information they supplied (for example, a scan of the benefit letter that proved their eligibility).
> Do not store personal information you do collect for longer than you need to given the purpose you collected it for. This will reduce opportunities for attackers to exploit security vulnerabilities in your service.

## 5. 9. Section G: Assurance > 9.6 The Use of Other IT Systems
Source: Orange Book: Management of Risk - Principles and Concepts (`orange-book`), HM Treasury. Authority: mandatory. page last updated 2026-07-29.
Cite inline as: ([Orange Book: Management of Risk - Principles and Concepts: 9.6 The Use of Other IT Systems](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/orange-book/the-orange-book-management-of-risk-principles-and-concepts#the-use-of-other-it-systems))

Obligations in this section (verbatim, strength from the modal verb):
- [RECOMMENDED] "Organisations should use whatever is most suitable for them."

Section text (verbatim):
> Various different systems are used for the purposes of assurance mapping and related risk and internal control assessment. Some are spreadsheet-based using reporting/visualisation tools and others are bespoke risk and control assessment and/ or auditing systems. Organisations should use whatever is most suitable for them. The RCoE’s assurance tool makes information available to organisations in Excel format which can be used as required.
